# Contributor lane guidance has no path when starter work is held

## Context

This is the lane-selection part of #14230's existing contributor journey. Following `CONTRIBUTING.md` on 7 November still names 13.2 as the next release and links closed milestone 9; current `ROADMAP.md` names 13.4 and its live milestone. The starter-label routes currently lead to held work, while the guide promises “there is always a way in” and offers no question route at that step. These are observations about the documented route, not a claim about how outside contributors arrive or why they leave.

## The Problem

A reader who has launched the engine needs a current release context and a next step when the listed tickets are already claimed or unsuitable. Merely replacing a release number leaves that second gap.

## The Architectural Reality

`CONTRIBUTING.md` §3 owns the route. `ROADMAP.md` owns current release scope and links its milestone; GitHub's existing Q&A category (`q-a`, public URL returned 200) owns the question door. No runtime or issue-assignment service change is needed. Prescription checked: `CONTRIBUTING.md` owns this guidance; changing the claim responder or Skills would not correct the stale release pointer and missing question route.

Design authority: #14230 facet 3 calls for wiring the existing Q&A door into a try-a-lane contribution path; #19105 requires linking the roadmap rather than copying its facts.

The prior decisions remain binding: #19201 rejected filtering these lists as a collision fix; #19194 deliberately permits unassigned PRs and retains first-approve-worthy semantics. Both stay unchanged.

## The Fix

Update this one guide section as a complete return route: follow the roadmap for release scope, retain the first-time/returning progression and existing claim policy, link Q&A when listed work is held or unsuitable, and require a new issue for a genuinely new problem rather than for finding existing work.

| Target surface | Source of authority | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Release pointer | `ROADMAP.md` | Follow its current milestone | The roadmap remains the durable entry | `CONTRIBUTING.md` §3 | Read current roadmap and rendered link |
| Starter-list return route | #14230 facet 3 | Existing label lists and first-time progression remain | Existing Q&A category when nothing fits | `CONTRIBUTING.md` §3 item 1 | Live queries/category and rendered first step |
| Claim and new-issue wording | #19194, #19201, #18999 | Keep claim paragraph and label URLs; new problems still need approval | Existing responder/maintainer path | `CONTRIBUTING.md` §3 items 2–3 | Base-relative comparison |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: The guide follows `ROADMAP.md` for the current release/milestone instead of fixing 13.2/milestone 9 in its prose.
- [ ] AC-2: Its starter step has a usable Q&A route for held or unsuitable work, without promising starter availability; first-time/returning progression remains.
- [ ] AC-3: Both label query URLs and the claim paragraph remain unchanged. The guide distinguishes a new problem needing an issue from choosing existing work, and still renders all seven contribution steps.

## Out of Scope

Starter-issue curation or reassignment; the retired #18985 event; claim-bot behavior; Skills audience/private-tool compatibility; instruction-file defaults and maintainer-home loading. Those remaining onboarding obligations stay on #14230.

## Avoided Traps

The initial uncommitted draft repeated #19201's rejected list filter and weakened #19194's claim rule. The closed-state sweep caught both; those draft changes were removed before publication. A fixed 13.4 link would repeat the next-release drift, so the guide follows the existing roadmap instead.
